split.name_en: Who has the right to vote
split.plus_en: The right to vote is held by more citizens, without conditions such as service or imprisonment
split.minus_en: The right to vote is conditioned or taken away from some citizens
split.statement_en: Every adult citizen should keep the right to vote, including those who did not do military or national service.

split.name_en: Voting access for people away from home
split.plus_en: Easier voting for people away from their home polling station
split.minus_en: Voting only at the home polling station, with stricter supervision
split.statement_en: Voting should be made easier for people away from home, such as soldiers and students, even if polling becomes harder to supervise.

reason: The heaviest bill (#1, about 22% of the weight, 15 initiators and 125 votes) conditions the right to vote on military or national service; with #11 (prisoners) it is about who may vote at all, not about convenience. A list can back that condition and still back easier voting for soldiers, so mixing it with the absentee-access bills (#2-#10, #14-#16, #18, #21, #24-#26, most of the remaining weight) blurs both positions. The current q88 text fits the access part unchanged. Left out as fitting neither part: voting by citizens living abroad (#12, #20, #22, #23), voting age (#17, #27), business owners voting in local elections (#13), referendum residents (#19), all light.
